checks.interpretation: No finite unconditional source-voltage disk is reported when calibration bounds are unknown.

classification: Modern synthetic inverse-problem fixture. Inferred effective voltage is not identification of dark matter, free energy, gravity or a historical Tesla theory.
limitations: Effective source location is not physical source identity
Calibration bounds are supplied assumptions, not measured performance
Rank calculations are finite model properties; real instruments require calibrated transfer functions
No dark-matter search sensitivity or detection significance is calculated
No cosmological field, stochastic detector noise, calibration drift, instrument transfer uncertainty beyond specified disk/M bounds, nonlinear material response or unmeasured additional port.
The 128 endpoint fixtures check a proven triangle-inequality disk; their inclusion is not statistical confidence or measured coverage.
At zero currents, the squared-amplitude Jacobians have rank zero; the nonlinear maps are not globally constant.
summary: Both calibrated, coherent complex-current channels reconstruct the two effective complex drive voltages; restricted readouts admit exact rival drives.
The injected 5 mV drive excludes zero only inside the supplied deterministic calibration model (nominal radius 1.932220 mV).
Channel phase error alone produces a receiver-drive residual when the true receiver drive is zero.
title: Which drive is visible? Phase readout and source localization
